children: , the leading dialysis providers in the U.S., traded lower on Tuesday after Axios reported that the Trump administration is planning to encourage competition within their market.

Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. is set to announce the plan in Fort Worth, Texas, today as part of a broader initiative aimed at battling chronic disease burden in the U.S., including chronic kidney disease.
The plan seeks to address what it identified as structural deficiencies in care and seeks changes to the dialysis market dominated by DaVita
as well as the transplant system.

The plan partly attributes some of the failures within the system to government overreach, noting that "in many cases, government should do less, focusing its efforts on promoting accountability, competition, and innovation."
The report calls for fewer barriers to entry within the dialysis space, where DaVita
control roughly 74% of the market. It also seeks better incentives and stricter oversight within the transplant system. Organ care provider TransMedics
